justification: Copy-only rename of a live public product name across 18 files. Not Minor: the tier floor caps Minor at 3 substantive files, and this touches 15 .ts/.tsx files including two copy-guard test suites that pinned the old wording. Not Critical: no logic, no data, no query, no schema and no route changes — every hunk is a user-visible string or a comment naming the product, and the diff is 59 insertions against 59 deletions with no net line change.

falsifiable_check.command: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/app/brief-copy-guards.test.ts __tests__/app/brief-unavailable-copy.test.ts && grep -rn -i 'intelligence brief' app components lib __tests__ COMPONENT_MAP.md; test $? -eq 1
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Either the two source-scan copy suites stop matching the strings they pin, or any frontend file still carries the retired product name in rendered copy, metadata, a JSX label or a comment that would mislead the next reader into re-splitting the naming.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Both halves were seen red. The grep half at origin/main printed 12 matching files including the exact reported defect, app/reports/layout.tsx:25 '{ href: /reports/intelligence-brief, label: Intelligence Brief }', plus app/internal/page.tsx:54 and components/reports/landing/data/intelligence-brief.ts:11 'Property Intelligence Brief'. The jest half printed 'Test Suites: 2 failed, 105 passed, 107 total / Tests: 3 failed, 1471 passed, 1474 total' mid-change, with brief-copy-guards.test.ts:44 failing on toContain for 'run the brief again to retry' — that is what surfaced the two backtick template literals a quoted-string sweep had missed. Green after: 107 suites / 1474 tests passed and the grep exits 1 with no output.

pre_impl.existing_data: The rename was already half-landed in the repo, so the work was to finish it rather than invent a name. app/reports/intelligence-brief/layout.tsx already had metadata title 'Property Site Report', page.tsx line 3013 already rendered an H1 of 'Site Report', app/site-directory/page.tsx:52 already labelled the link 'Site Report', app/how-it-works/page.tsx:15 already listed the tool as 'Site Report', and app/api/canibuildit/lead/route.ts:514 already sent an email subject of 'Your Site Report'. The new strings were taken from those five existing surfaces, not chosen fresh.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The assumption that would have broken this is that a rename is one grep for the full phrase. It is not: the majority of the stale copy said plain 'brief' rather than 'Intelligence Brief' — 'Generate Brief', 'What the Brief Covers', 'Brief generation failed', 'New brief', 'run the brief again to retry', 'Typical brief'. A first sweep also missed two occurrences inside backtick template literals in unavailable.ts because the search pattern only matched single- and double-quoted strings; the full jest run is what surfaced them.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new file, component, script or lint was added. The guard against recurrence already existed — __tests__/app/brief-copy-guards.test.ts and __tests__/app/brief-unavailable-copy.test.ts are source-scan copy tests over exactly these modules — so the existing suites were updated to pin the new strings rather than a parallel terminology lint being written. Route paths, API paths, component names, module filenames and the interest_type value 'intelligence-brief' stored on lead rows were deliberately left alone: they are identifiers, and renaming them would break live links and already-stored rows.

functions.name: describeUnavailable
functions.input: A nullable reason string recorded against a missing field, plus the section key and an optional human name for the layer that was being fetched.
functions.output: An object of label, detail and tone whose detail string is rendered directly to the user; four of its branches carried the retired product noun and now say 'report' instead.
functions.if_none: When the reason is null or unrecognised the function falls through to the catch-all retrieval-miss branch, which still tells the reader to run the report again rather than claiming the field was never promised.

functions.name: ReportsLayout
functions.input: The React children for any page under /reports; the nav it renders is driven by the module-level NAV_ITEMS array declared at line 24.
functions.output: The dark public header whose first nav entry is the reported defect — it linked /reports/intelligence-brief under the label 'Intelligence Brief' and now renders 'Site Report'.
functions.if_none: NAV_ITEMS is a static literal, so there is no empty or loading case; a missing entry would simply not render a link, and the href is unchanged so every existing bookmark still resolves.

values: N/A — no value is read from a database, an API or an optional field by this change; every hunk is a literal string in source.
queries: N/A — no SQL, no Supabase call and no fetch was added, removed or altered.

break_it.scenario: A reader lands on the landing hero from the /reports header, sees one product name in the nav and a different one in the H1 below it, and concludes the link took them somewhere else.
break_it.what_happens: That was the reported defect: the nav said Intelligence Brief while the page H1 and the route metadata already said Site Report.
break_it.how: NAV_ITEMS label, the ProductLandingV2 hero title and ctaLabel, and the page H1 now all read Site Report, sourced from the metadata that was already correct.
break_it.repro: Open the Vercel preview at /reports and read the first entry in the dark header nav against the H1 on the page it opens.

break_it.scenario: A run fails or times out and the user reads the error path, which is the surface least likely to be re-read after a rename.
break_it.what_happens: The error copy would still have named the retired product — 'Failed to start intelligence brief', 'Brief generation failed', 'The brief is still queued' — reintroducing the split name at the exact moment the reader is confused.
break_it.how: The three error strings in page.tsx and the JSON error in app/api/intelligence-brief/route.ts were renamed together, and the full jest run covers the route.
break_it.repro: On /reports/intelligence-brief, submit an address the geocoder cannot resolve and read the red error panel; or curl -X POST /api/intelligence-brief with an empty body and read the JSON error field.

break_it.scenario: A field cannot be retrieved and the unavailable-label classifier renders its retry copy, which lives in a separate module from the page.
break_it.what_happens: Two of those strings are backtick template literals, so a naive quoted-string sweep skipped them and left 'run the brief again to retry' rendering under a page titled Site Report.
break_it.how: The full jest run went red on brief-copy-guards.test.ts and brief-unavailable-copy.test.ts, which pin that copy by source scan; both template literals were fixed and both suites updated to assert the new wording.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/app/brief-unavailable-copy.test.ts — it calls describeUnavailable with an unrecognised reason and with 'timeout', which are the two branches whose detail strings are template literals.

break_it.scenario: Someone renames the stored lead interest_type or the /reports/intelligence-brief route to match the new product name.
break_it.what_happens: Live links from the funnel pages, the site directory, how-it-works and the already-sent lead emails would 404, and existing rows carrying interest_type 'intelligence-brief' would stop matching the email-template switch at app/api/canibuildit/lead/route.ts:514.
break_it.how: No route, API path, component name, module filename or interest_type value was touched — the diff is labels and comments only, and every href in the tree still points at /reports/intelligence-brief.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && grep -rn 'reports/intelligence-brief' app components lib — every href must still be the unchanged route; then grep -rn "interest_type === 'intelligence-brief'" app/api/canibuildit/lead/route.ts for the stored-value switch.

break_it.scenario: A future session reads a stale comment such as 'Secondary Dwelling card for the Intelligence Brief' and re-splits the naming by following the comment instead of the rendered copy.
break_it.what_happens: That is how the original split arose — the H1 was renamed while the nav, the landing config and the surrounding comments kept the old name.
break_it.how: The product-naming comments in provenance.ts, unavailable.ts, page.tsx, ConstraintArithmeticCard.tsx, GrannyFlatBriefCard.tsx and COMPONENT_MAP.md were renamed in the same commit, so the grep in falsifiable_check returns zero across code and docs together.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && grep -rn -i 'intelligence brief' app components lib __tests__ COMPONENT_MAP.md — zero matches means no stale comment is left to mislead the next reader.

post_merge.db_reset: None — no migration, no backfill and no row is read or written by this change.
post_merge.secrets: None — no environment variable, key or credential is added, read or changed.
post_merge.other_repo: None — the change is confined to frontend-nextjs in this repository; the Python services carry the old name only in docstrings, log lines and an LLM system prompt, none of which reach a user.
post_merge.manual_verify: On the Vercel preview, open /reports and confirm the first header nav entry reads Site Report and still opens /reports/intelligence-brief; then submit a bad address and confirm the error panel reads 'Report generation failed' rather than 'Brief generation failed'.
